newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU centrists reaffirm commitment to EMU on time.
newsitem.headline: EU centrists reaffirm commitment to EMU on time.

text.p: Leaders of the European Union's (EU) centrist governments reaffirmed their commitment on Tuesday to ensuring that economic and monetary union (EMU) would start on time in January, 1999.

"It is clear coming from this meeting that the objective and political will...exists to start the single currency on time," Irish Prime Minister John Bruton told reporters at a summit of the European People's Party, a mainly Christian Democrat group.

Bruton, attending the meeting with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Italian Premier Romano Prodi and Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, played down market fears that EMU could be delayed as EU members grappled with qualification criteria.
"I don't believe postponement will occur. (EMU) will happen on time, with Ireland taking part," a report prepared for Wednesday's Irish Times newspaper quoted Bruton as saying.

Warning against any fudging on EMU qualification, Aznar reiterated that treaty requirements for EMU must be respected. "There is a treaty and there is a (EMU) timetable to respect," he told reporters in the wings of the meeting.
A number of EU states are struggling to curb budget deficits, raising questions over whether EMU will start on time in 1999.
Aznar said EMU had not been allowed to dominate the meeting which also covered progress on other key EU issues such as closer cooperation on justice and home affairs.
Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker earlier warned against putting back the January 1, 1999 start date.
"It is not a good idea to delay EMU," he said, noting that the old European Community once delayed a plan for a defence union and that it had never since seen the light of day.
